newsitem.title: UK: Catholic injured as bomb explodes in Belfast.
newsitem.headline: Catholic injured as bomb explodes in Belfast.

text.p: A 25-year-old Catholic man was injured on Sunday when his car exploded in the Ardoyne Irish nationalist area of north Belfast, residents said.

No one immediately claimed responsibility for the blast, which came less than 48 hours after the IRA raised fears of a new cycle of violence in Northern Ireland by shooting a policeman guarding a prominent pro-British Protestant politician.

Bobby Lavery, a local councillor for Sinn Fein, the political wing of the Irish Republican Army, named the injured man as Eddie Copeland, a well-known member of the republican movement opposed to British rule. He said he had been taken to hospital with serious leg injuries.
"The windows were blown out in houses next door," Lavery told reporters as British troops and armed police stood guard by the man's damaged car.

A senior police officer said it seemed there had been "a localised explosion", possibly beneath the driver's seat. Joe Hendron, the local member of parliament, said he feared the apparent car bomb was in retaliation for Friday's shooting.

Lavery put the blame on extremist pro-British Protestant gunmen and the largely Protestant Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC). Asked who he thought was responsible, he replied: "I think it was a mixture of Loyalist paramilitaries and the RUC."
